note: Editable rules for source-finder layer 3 (Jerome). Like ledger-allowlist.json, this is data, not code: change a number or a pattern here and the next run uses it. Patterns are regular expressions matched against the page text after lowercasing and removing accents, and only when they appear within `window` characters of the subject's name. Layer 3 finds EVIDENCE for a person to look at; it never proves anything, and when unsure it asks (review). Items marked PROVISIONAL are Claude's starting values and have not been confirmed by Tom.

sufficiency._note: CONFIRMED: Tom wants plenty of material, judged by quality not by number of sites. minWords is the floor (ready); targetWords is the goal (Jerome runs a second allowlist search until it is reached or the fetch caps run out; below it a ready entry is flagged thin_material). Both count only SUBSTANTIVE pages: verify-capable pages where the subject's name appears at least minMentionsPerPage times. targetWords (4000) and minMentionsPerPage (3) are PROVISIONAL. CONFIRMED in principle: one verify-capable source can be enough. minWordsVerifyCapable is PROVISIONAL (about twice the target article length). newSubjectMinDomains is PROVISIONAL: raise to 2 to require two independent verify-capable websites before a brand-new subject (for example a visitor suggestion) can proceed. Reported-tier and unjudged pages never count toward this.

perspectives._note: Perspective lanes (Tom's rule): do not stop at one kind of site. Different sites have different strengths, so after the word target is met Jerome also looks for any lane that this category should have but does not yet. A lane is COVERED when approved pages on its sites, really about the subject, total at least minWordsPerLane. Lanes marked contextOnly count as perspective (theology, reflection) but can never verify a claim: the registry rule that reported-tier sources never count as verified still applies. Sites are listed by domain; {domain, pathPrefix} limits a site to part of it (New Advent hosts the Encyclopedia, the Fathers and the Summa under different paths). Only sites that are ENABLED in ledger-allowlist.json are ever searched. PROVISIONAL: every list, order and number here is Claude's starting guess for Tom to edit.

perspectives._searchesPerLane: Web searches one perspective-lane search may use (the default for any search is 3). Found on the Akita run: two lane searches on sites with nothing about the subject used 6 searches ($0.06) and found no usable page. One search per lane keeps the lane idea and cuts that waste. PROVISIONAL.

selection._note: Selection (Tom's rule): Jerome searches a wide pool, then hands the writer only the best few. poolTarget = how many substantive approved pages Jerome tries to gather before it stops hunting (it still stops at the fetch caps). maxSelected / targetSelected = the best 4 are provided; fewer than 3 is flagged few_sources. Picks run lane by lane in the category's priority order (so the 4 are different KINDS of source), then fill by score. At most maxPerDomain pages from one site and maxContextOnly context-only (reported-tier) pages; at least one verify-capable page is always included if any exists. A page's score = words (up to maxWordsCredited) + how often the name appears (up to maxMentionsCredited) + name in the title + the tier weight. The floor and target word checks (sufficiency) apply to the SELECTED pages only: if only one page qualifies, its word count must pass the floor on its own. PROVISIONAL: every number here is Claude's starting guess.

authorityLookup._note: Tom's idea: for an apparition or miracle, Jerome also finds the OFFICIAL website of the diocese whose bishop judges it, because that bishop's statement is the authority for its approval. Jerome only PROPOSES: code fetches the page and checks it names the diocese and reads like a church site, then the site is put in ignatius-queue.json as waiting. IGNATIUS (not built yet) decides and approves; nothing here edits the registry. Costs one extra model call with up to maxSearches web searches (about $0.02-0.04). Set enabled to false to switch it off, or add a category letter to the list.

_fetchBlockedDomains: Sites that answered Jerome's automated fetches with HTTP 403 in the first live run (britannica.com, kids.britannica.com). They are never searched or counted, and a perspective lane whose only sites are blocked is dropped (so the independent-check lane is out until a fetchable site is chosen). Add a domain here whenever a live run shows 403s from it. PROVISIONAL.
_genericNameWords: Words skipped when choosing the part of a name that evidence must appear near (so "Miracle of Lanciano" is anchored on "lanciano"). PROVISIONAL starter list.

scandal._note: CONFIRMED: scandals go to review. This list is only a net for obvious names (checked against the subject's name, not the page text). Whether an entry IS a scandal is a judgment; the real recognition is Ignatius's job later. PROVISIONAL starter list for Tom to edit.

s.label: Saint
s._note: CONFIRMED: three bases. A basis counts only if its evidence appears near the saint's name on a source that can verify. PROVISIONAL: the pattern lists and the year limits.

ancient_veneration._note: Before the first papal canonization (993) sainthood meant early, wide, continuous veneration, so this basis looks for DIFFERENT KINDS of evidence, not for one phrase. Each signal type has a strength. Accepted when at least minDistinctTypes different types are found near the name and at least minStrong of them are strong, and none of the cautions appear. One kind alone, or only weak signals, goes to review. Types are counted, not pages: ten sites repeating one claim are one signal. decisiveTypes lists any type that is enough by itself (empty now; for example ["liturgical"] would let a Roman Martyrology entry alone settle it). Weak signals (patronage, place and hospital names) never count towards the strong requirement. The text cannot tell whether a church dedication is early or modern, which is why dedications are only medium. PROVISIONAL: every pattern and number is Claude's starting guess.

ancient_veneration._siteSignals: Some evidence is WHERE a page lives, not what it says: an Orthodox site does not write 'the Orthodox Church commemorates him', it simply has its own entry for him. A verify-capable page on one of these sites, whose web address contains the saint's name (nameInSlug) and which names him at least minMentions times (default 1), counts as that signal type. Found on the first Pachomius run: the OCA entry (29 mentions) and Vatican News's saint-of-the-day page. Vatican News counts only as a feast day (medium), not as the Roman Martyrology, because it also lists local and recent saints. Known limit: a namesake saint's page can match (augustine-of-canterbury for Augustine of Hippo). PROVISIONAL.
ancient_veneration._cautions: TIGHTENED 2026-10-09 after the first Pachomius run: the bare words 'legendary' and 'historicity' matched a translator's note about a legendary ANGEL in the Lausiac History and blocked a saint venerated for 1,600 years. A caution now has to say something about the person or the calendar.

notCanonized._note: Used only when NO basis was found. Signals that the person may be Blessed, Venerable or a Servant of God: review, reason 'not canonized'.
